title: Drop Biscuits and Sausage Gravy
source: Biscuits adapted from America's Test Kitchen drop biscuits; gravy rewritten from their all-purpose gravy as a sausage cream gravy
yield: 12 biscuits and about 3 cups gravy — 6 servings
millSetting: fine — placeholder, not yet dialed in
note: Drop biscuits, not rolled — no cutting, no folding, no rest. The melted butter is supposed to seize into clumps in the cold buttermilk; those clumps are 20% water and steam the biscuits upward. Smooth batter makes flat biscuits.
milling: Soft white is the berry here — lowest protein, tenderest crumb. Mill both flour weights at once and let the flour come to room temperature before mixing; it leaves the Mockmill warm, and warm flour melts the butter clumps the biscuits depend on. Fresh-milled absorbs liquid slowly, so the batter stiffens as it sits — scoop promptly and keep extra buttermilk within reach. Bran interrupts gluten and browns early: check the biscuits at 11 minutes. In the gravy, whole-grain flour thickens slightly slower per gram and keeps tightening off the heat, so pull it looser than you want it. Store milled flour in the freezer and use within a week.
substitute: Store-bought: 283 g unbleached all-purpose flour for the biscuits, 40 g for the gravy. Skip the extra buttermilk allowance — refined flour hits final hydration immediately.

ingredients.item: unsalted butter, melted and cooled slightly

ingredients.note: sage-forward; casings removed if using links
only if the sausage renders less than ~50 g fat
the sausage is already salty — taste first

steps: Mill 328 g soft white flour total — 283 g for the biscuits, 45 g for the gravy. Spread it on a sheet pan and let it cool to room temperature. Heat the oven to 475°F with a rack in the middle and line a rimmed baking sheet with parchment.
Whisk the 283 g flour, baking powder, sugar, salt, and baking soda together in a large bowl.
Stir the 113 g melted butter into the cold buttermilk until the butter seizes into small clumps. Leave them — do not stir them smooth.
Fold the buttermilk into the dry ingredients with a spatula and stop the moment the batter pulls away from the bowl. If it's too stiff to release from a scoop, work in buttermilk 10 g at a time.

Scoop 12 level ¼-cup portions onto the sheet, spaced 1½ inches apart. Bake until the tops are golden and crisp, 11 to 14 minutes. Brush with the remaining 28 g melted butter and cool 5 minutes on a rack.
While the biscuits bake, brown the sausage in a large skillet over medium-high heat, breaking it into bite-size crumbles, 7 to 8 minutes. Leave the browned bits stuck to the pan.

You want about 50 g fat in the skillet — pour off any excess or add the 28 g butter to make it up. Reduce to medium, scatter the 45 g flour over the sausage, and cook, stirring constantly, until it smells toasted, about 2 minutes.

Whisk in the milk in three additions, scraping the fond loose as you go. Simmer, stirring often, until the gravy coats a spoon, 8 to 10 minutes. Pepper heavily, then salt to taste. Split the biscuits and spoon the gravy over.
